interactions.note: The affinity of epitope-specific mAb CD6 for binding the neuraminidase from influenza A virus (A/California/07/2009(H1N1)) was determined with a Biolayer Interferometry Octet Red system.

The epitope-specific mAb CD6 bound to neuraminidase from influenza A virus (A/California/07/2009(H1N1)), expressed on transfected 293T cells. Point mutation of 15 residues that differ between NA from CA/09 and BR/07 showed that no single mutation completely abolished binding. Mutation D451G reduced binding to <10% and the double mutation N449D/D451G abolished CD6 binding. This double mutant was also selected as an escape variant with CD6 and H6N1 (CA/09). The point mutation S95N, but not S95A, reduced binding, suggesting the bulky Asn group disrupted binding to other residues in this region.

The epitope for Fab 18_14D on the N6 head domain monomer was determined by single particle reconstruction cryo-electron microscopy of the ternary complex of Fabs 18_14D and 1G01 bound to N6_DQ at an overall resolution of 3.2 Å with focused refinement to 3.0 Å.

The epitope of Mem5 Fab on neuraminidase (NA) of influenza virus A/Memphis/31/98 (H3N2) was determined from the crystal structure of the complex. Data were collected at room temperature to 3.0 Å [PDB: 2AEQ] and from frozen crystals to 2.1 Å resolution [PDB: 2AEP]. The epitope is located on loops surrounding the active site cavity but on the opposite side to the N9 epitopes recognized by NC41 and NC10. Carbohydrate attached to Asn200 residue of the antigen forms part of the epitope.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 2.1 angstroms
